title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from p.146. E and K are arbitrary, possibly infinite, algebraic extensions of Q. Fix an algebraic closure Qbar with G = Gal(Qbar/Q). Let I_E = Hom(E, Qbar) and I_K = Hom(K, Qbar); these are profinite homogeneous G-sets. An ideal A of E⊗_Q K is the same as a G-invariant clopen subset Σ of I_E × I_K, with G acting diagonally. Write Σ' for its complement.

The CM condition from p.146 is stated fibrewise. Pick y ∈ I_K, i.e. an embedding K ⊂ Qbar, and put Σ_y = Σ ∩ (I_E × {y}). The condition is (τ×1)Σ_y = Σ'_y for every complex conjugation τ ∈ G. Concretely, Σ_y ⊂ Hom(E, Qbar) is a 'CM type with values in K': every conjugation swaps Σ_y with its complement.

Step 1 (this page). The condition does not depend on y. Since Σ_{gy} = (g×g)Σ_y and g^{-1}τg is again a conjugation, the condition can be written globally as (τ×1)Σ = Σ' for all conjugations τ.

Step 2. It is equivalent to (1×τ)Σ = Σ'. Grothendieck first writes ⊂, then proves =. The proof: G-invariance gives (τ×τ)Σ = Σ, hence (1×τ)Σ = (τ×1)(τ×τ)Σ = (τ×1)Σ = Σ'.

Conclusion: 'la condition envisagée est symétrique en E, K'. A CM type on E with values in K is the same thing as a CM type on K with values in E. This is the symmetric, correspondence-style formulation of the Shimura–Taniyama duality between a CM type (E, Φ) and its reflex.

Crossed-out attempt. He tries to describe the field of definition K_0 ⊂ K of the ideal (the reflex field) as the fixed field of a subgroup H ⊂ G. H is defined via those g with (g×1)Σ_y = Σ_y, and he checks independence of y. He abandons this, probably as too messy.

NB paragraph.
- A CM ('Shimura–Taniyama') structure A on (E, K) extends to A' = A·(E'⊗K') for any extensions E ⊂ E', K ⊂ K'.
- Conversely, regarded as an ideal of E_K, A has a field of definition K_0 ⊂ K that is invariant under extension of K (trivial verification).
- By the E/K symmetry the same holds on the E side.

The next page derives from this a smallest pair (E_0, K_0) of definition: the CM field and its reflex field, with [K_0:Q] ≤ binom(2d, d). It then introduces CM bimodules and the reflex-norm homomorphism of tori Ψ_Σ: T_K → T_E, Ψ_Σ(x) = det_{t/E}(x).

Purpose: building the Galois-theoretic / Tannakian framework for CM motives ('Théorie de Galois des motifs', 1965). Taking E and K large (e.g. Q^cm), the system of all such Σ and the tori maps leads to what is now the Serre group, i.e. the motivic Galois group of CM motives.
errors: Minor: the first equivalent form is written with '⊂' ((1×τ)Σ ⊂ Σ') while the proof yields equality. Both are equivalent here, since (1×τ) is a bijection preserving fibre structure and Σ ⊂ Σ' is impossible. Harmless.

The reduction to y-independence is asserted as 'évident'. The needed fact is that conjugates g^{-1}τg of complex conjugations are again complex conjugations, i.e. the set of conjugations is a conjugacy-stable set. True, but unstated.
The crossed-out description of K_0 as the fixed field of H is muddled: it mixes (g×1) and (g×g) actions and is not completed on this page.

ideas.what: Encoding a CM type with values in K as a G-invariant clopen subset Σ ⊂ Hom(E,Qbar)×Hom(K,Qbar), equivalently an ideal of E⊗_Q K, allowing infinite extensions
ideas.modern_name: CM type as an idempotent/ideal of E⊗K; generalized CM types / CM correspondences
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura–Taniyama (CM types, 1961); the tensor-product/idempotent formulation is standard in Serre (Abelian l-adic representations, 1968), Deligne (Hodge cycles on abelian varieties, LNM 900) and Milne's notes

ideas.what: Symmetry of the CM condition in E and K: (τ×1)Σ=Σ' iff (1×τ)Σ=Σ', so a CM type on E with values in K is a CM type on K with values in E
ideas.modern_name: Duality between a CM type and its reflex (reflex of reflex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Shimura–Taniyama; Shimura 'Abelian varieties with complex multiplication'

ideas.what: Field of definition of the ideal, compatible with extension of scalars; existence of a smallest pair (E_0, K_0)
ideas.modern_name: CM field generated by the type and its reflex field

missed.claim: Grothendieck in 1965 reformulates CM types symmetrically as clopen G-invariant subsets of I_E×I_K (ideals in E⊗K, for arbitrary algebraic extensions) as groundwork for a Galois theory of CM motives. This anticipates the Serre-group / Taniyama-group framework (Serre 1968; Deligne, Langlands, Milne–Shih c.1979–82). It is historically interesting evidence of early independent work, but the mathematics itself is classical.
missed.quote: Donc la condition envisagée est symétrique en E, K.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: documents that Grothendieck was working out the CM part of the motivic Galois group, via reflex norms of tori, already in 1965. No new mathematics for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, clean, but classical: the symmetric ideal-theoretic formulation of CM types and their reflex duality is standard (Shimura–Taniyama, Serre, Deligne). Its interest is mainly historical, as an early Grothendieck approach to CM motives.
